title: v4 watchdog: restart dead daemons, report spawn failures and stalled queues; resolve the claude CLI without PATH
spec:
Stall watchdog and the PATH root cause.

Root cause first: worker spawns run the `claude` CLI found on the daemon's PATH; a daemon started from a shell without the
Homebrew bin dir failed every spawn with "claude CLI not found on PATH" (luna-inbox review T-0599, 2026-10-06).
1. Resolve the CLI once per spawn: shutil.which("claude") on PATH, else the first existing of
   /opt/homebrew/bin/claude, /usr/local/bin/claude, ~/.local/bin/claude, ~/.claude/local/claude; pass the absolute path.
   Find every place that spawns claude (grep orchestrator/ for "claude" in subprocess argv) and route them through one helper.
2. New orchestrator/watchdog.py and CLI `orchestrator watchdog [--once] [--install-launchd]`, machine level:
   - Repos to watch: every repo with a .orchestrator/daemon.lock known to the machine registry (~/.orchestrator-machine,
     orchestrator/machine.py) or listed in [watchdog].repos of the orchestrator's pool.toml.
   - Every 5 minutes per repo: (a) daemon alive = its daemon.lock is held (fcntl test, no write); if not and the repo has
     queued/running/held tasks or an open goal -> start `uv run orchestrator daemon` with ORCH_ROOT=<repo> and a PATH that
     includes the Homebrew bin dir, log to <repo>/.orchestrator/runs/daemon-<ts>.log, notify once;
     (b) a task "running" for more than 2x its timeout_s with no live worker pid -> let the daemon's reconcile_dead handle it
     if the daemon is alive, else count it as stalled; (c) spawn failures in the last 30 minutes of bus events
     ("not found on PATH", spawn error) -> notify once with the error; (d) nothing dispatched, gated or merged for 60 min
     while ready tasks exist and accounts are not cooling -> notify once "queue stalled".
   - Notifications through notify.notify_once with keys per repo+condition, so each condition is reported once until it clears.
   - --install-launchd prints (does not write) a LaunchAgent plist that runs `orchestrator watchdog` every 300 s, and the
     two commands the human runs to load it; installing it is the human's step.
3. The machine registry gains the repo path when a daemon acquires its lock (machine.py), so new repos are watched automatically.
Tests tests/test_watchdog.py (temp repos, fake clock, no real daemons: patch the start function): test_claude_resolved_without_path_entry,
test_restarts_dead_daemon_with_work, test_no_restart_without_work, test_reports_spawn_failure_once, test_reports_stalled_queue_once,
test_registry_adds_repo_on_lock, test_install_launchd_prints_only.


AMENDMENTS from spec review T-1672 (v3). Where they differ from the text above, the amendments win.
W1 Registry: add `register_repo(path)` and `repos()` to orchestrator/machine.py storing ~/.orchestrator-machine/repos.json
   (under the existing machine lock). Call register_repo from daemon.acquire_lock right after the lock is taken
   (orchestrator/daemon.py is in scope for this one call). [watchdog].repos in the orchestrator's pool.toml adds extra paths.
W2 Watchdog notifications: its own dedupe file ~/.orchestrator-machine/watchdog-state.json, keyed "<repo>:<condition>",
   storing first_seen and notified_at; a condition is reported once and again only after it cleared and came back.
   Send via notify.notify (not notify_once). The watchdog never writes to any repo's bus.
W3 Resolver everywhere: one helper orchestrator/claude_cli.py `resolve() -> str | None` used by spawn.py (both the which
   check ~1336 and the Popen ~1365 path), goals.py ~350 and planner_shadow.py ~33; add those three files to scope. If no
   candidate exists, keep the existing hold but with the reason "claude CLI not found; looked in: <list>".
W4 Lock probe: open daemon.lock with os.open(path, os.O_RDONLY) (create nothing, truncate nothing); flock LOCK_SH|LOCK_NB;
   if it succeeds the daemon is dead: release immediately, then start the daemon and, before notifying, confirm within 20 s
   that the lock is held by the new daemon. Missing lock file = never had a daemon: only start it if the repo is registered.
W5 Data for (b) and (d): read tasks from <repo>/.orchestrator/tasks/*.json directly (read-only). Running too long:
   status running, now - pipeline.dispatched_at > 2 * constraints.timeout_s (defaults 900), and the daemon is dead.
   Stalled queue: at least one queued execute task whose depends_on are all merged, no task file modified in the last
   60 min (mtime of tasks/*.json), and machine.py account state shows no account cooling. Name these predicates as
   functions with unit tests.
Extra tests: test_lock_probe_readonly_and_released, test_dedupe_reports_again_after_clear, test_resolver_used_by_goals_and_shadow,
test_running_too_long_only_when_daemon_dead, test_registry_written_on_acquire_lock.


AMENDMENTS v4 from spec review T-1677 (final; sent to the builder without another spec review; the post-gate security
review still applies). Where they differ from everything above, these win.
X1 Cooling: read each repo's own pool state file written by orchestrator/pool.py (find its path and cooldown fields there;
   read-only); "not cooling" = no account cooldown in the future. machine.py account data is not used for this.
X2 Daemon alive without touching the lock: daemon.acquire_lock writes "<pid>\n" into daemon.lock after taking the lock
   (truncate + write on the already-open fd). The watchdog reads the pid, alive = os.kill(pid, 0) succeeds and
   `ps -o command= -p <pid>` contains "orchestrator" and "daemon". No flock probe at all (drop W4's probe).
X3 Single instance: the watchdog takes LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB on ~/.orchestrator-machine/watchdog.lock for its run; if held it
   exits 0 silently.
X4 Proof of one resolver: a test greps orchestrator/*.py and fails if any file other than claude_cli.py builds a
   subprocess argv whose first element is the literal "claude".
X5 Spawn failures: read-only scan of <repo>/.orchestrator/tasks/*.json for hold_reason or reason containing
   "claude CLI not found", "not found on PATH" or "spawn" updated in the last 30 min.
X6 uv: resolve uv like claude (which, then /opt/homebrew/bin/uv, ~/.local/bin/uv, ~/.cargo/bin/uv); the printed launchd
   plist sets PATH with the Homebrew bin dir first.
X7 Registry: missing repo dirs are skipped and pruned from repos.json on each run; never start a daemon for them.
X8 Dedupe: each run first evaluates every condition for every repo, then clears state keys whose condition is false and
   drops keys of pruned repos, then notifies new ones.
X9 Tests patch machine.MACHINE_DIR and every derived path, and the watchdog state/lock paths, to temp dirs.
Extra tests: test_alive_by_pid_file_no_flock, test_second_watchdog_exits, test_no_literal_claude_argv_outside_resolver,
test_spawn_failure_from_task_files, test_uv_resolved_without_path, test_missing_repo_pruned, test_clear_pass_drops_keys,
test_cooling_from_repo_pool_state.
acceptance: tests/test_watchdog.py: the seven named tests exist and pass
every claude spawn goes through one resolver helper
--install-launchd prints and writes nothing outside the repo

constraints.note: c5 on purpose: three spec review rounds done (T-1666/T-1671/T-1676 or T-1672/T-1677); Planner folded the last findings; security review after the gate still runs

result.summary:
The watchdog and the single claude resolver are in and committed on `task/T-1679` (2 commits). All 20 tests in `tests/test_watchdog.py` pass. One existing test, `test_spawn::test_run_claude_holds_when_cli_missing`, now fails on this machine. It's outside my write scope, so the full gate won't be green until someone edits it.

**What changed**
- **Resolver:** new `orchestrator/claude_cli.py` finds `claude` on PATH, then in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `~/.local/bin` and `~/.claude/local`. `resolve_uv()` does the same for `uv`. All three places that start claude (`spawn.py`, `goals.py`, `planner_shadow.py`) now get the path from it.
  - `spawn.py` puts the absolute path first in the command. `goals.py` and `planner_shadow.py` keep the literal `claude` first and pass the path as Popen's `executable`, because an existing goals test checks for the literal.
  - If claude isn't found anywhere, the task is held with "claude CLI not found; looked in: …".
  - A test fails if any other file builds a command that starts with a literal `"claude"`.
- **Daemon lock:** `acquire_lock` now writes its pid into `daemon.lock` and adds the repo to `~/.orchestrator-machine/repos.json`. It also opens the file in append mode instead of `"w"`, so a second daemon that loses the lock no longer wipes the running daemon's pid.
- **Registry:** `machine.py` gains `register_repo`, `repos` and `prune_repos`, all under the existing machine lock.
- **Watchdog:** new `orchestrator/watchdog.py` and `orchestrator watchdog [--once] [--install-launchd]`.
  - It only reads each repo's files and never writes to any repo's bus. It doesn't touch `daemon.lock`: a daemon counts as alive if the pid in that file is running and `ps` shows an orchestrator daemon.
  - It restarts a dead daemon when there is work (or the repo is registered), with the Homebrew bin dir first on PATH, and checks for up to 20 s that the new daemon came up.
  - It reports four things: a dead daemon, tasks running past 2× their timeout while the daemon is dead, spawn failures in task files from the last 30 min, and a stalled queue. "Stalled" means a ready task, no task file changed for 60 min, and no account or Codex cooldown in the repo's `pool_state.json`.
  - Each problem is notified once, and again only after it clears and comes back. Repos whose folder is gone are dropped from the registry. Only one watchdog runs at a time.
  - `--install-launchd` prints a plist (run every 300 s) and the two `launchctl` commands for you to run. It writes nothing.
- **Your call on two loose definitions:**
  - "Open goal" means a record in `runs/goals.json` that isn't exited, stopped, done, failed or closed.
  - The spawn-failure check matches the word "spawn" anywhere in a task's hold reason, as the spec says, which may be too broad.

**Files changed**
`orchestrator/claude_cli.py` (new), `orchestrator/watchdog.py` (new), `orchestrator/spawn.py`, `orchestrator/goals.py`, `orchestrator/planner_shadow.py`, `orchestrator/daemon
